text:
ana: quick heads-up — after the quant4 bring-up for mag13b-v2 on dedicated, we're seeing a regression in long-window behavior. fill-rate drops ~3.2% on our longchain benchmark and KV cache starts to diverge around token ~4096. sharing logs.
ben: hmm, was this observed only under int4 quant or also int8 baseline?
ana: only after int4 quantization + new packing. int8 baseline (gold) doesn't show it.
chandra: can you paste the exact command you used to run the bench?
ana: sure:
```
./run_longchain_bench --model mag13b-v2.quant4 --seq 8192 --prefill 6144 --batch 4 --kv-mode streaming --seed 42
```
ana: short excerpt from the trace where we start to diverge (KV index vs tokens):
```
[4092] kv_index=0x7f8a... expected_hash=0x3a1f got=0x2b9c
[4096] kv_index=0x7f8a... expected_hash=0x4b2e got=0x4b2e
[4097] kv_index=0x7f8a... expected_hash=0x5c3d got=0x1a0f
```
sam: that pattern looks like an off-by-one in the ROPE wrapping or a stride mismatch when we compact int4 words. Did we change prefill stride logic in the quant packing PR?
liz: I reviewed PR #872 (quant packing). It adjusted prefill alignment to 32-byte boundaries which affects memcpy offsets. Could cause misaligned loads in fused kernels on a few GPUs.
ben: possible. can we repro deterministic with a single seed + single gpu? if so I can attach debugger.
ana: repro is stable on my dev A100 with seed 42; failing 9/10 runs. will drop a minimal reproducer.
chandra: another angle — could this be RoPE frequency scaling mismatch after quantization? If the rotary keys are reconstructed with reduced precision, phase wrap thresholds might shift at long positions.
sam: good point. compare kv keys before and after quant: run a dump of rotary sin/cos multipliers and sample at positions 4000..4100.
ana: did that. differences show tiny relative errors (~1e-5) until 4096 then jump to ~1e-2 for some channels.
bench-bot: benchmark run queued: longchain-fillrate/v2 on mag13b-v2.quant4 (seq=8192, batch=4).
eval-bot: sanity-eval: f1_longwindow (gold) = 0.873, current = 0.843, delta = -0.030.
ben: that delta is larger than expected for rounding noise. If packing changed base pointer alignment, some vector loads could read shifted words => catastrophic in some lanes.
liz: I can spin a test that forces unaligned memcpy path and one that forces aligned. if difference shows up that narrows it down.
chandra: also check kernel selection logic: quantized kernels choose a different codepath above sequence threshold. maybe a new heuristic triggers at 4096 and uses a fused path with different assumptions.
sam: good call. add logs for kernel variant and path: `LOG=DEBUG KERNEL_PATH=1 ./run...`
ana: done: attaching variant log (snippet):
```
[4090] kernel_variant=kv_fused_pack_v2
[4096] kernel_variant=kv_fused_pack_v3
```
ana: v2 -> v3 transition exactly at wrap point.
ben: ok that explains the step change. v3 likely assumes 16B-aligned tiles; v2 was tolerant. if quant packing moved the base pointer, v3's vectorized loads get garbage in some lanes.
liz: I'll add a temporary guard to force v2 and run the bench.
bench-bot: benchmark result: fillrate=0.872 (forced v2) — matches gold within noise :thumbsup:
ana: hotpatch confirms hypothesis. thanks! next steps:
- liz to add alignment-check + safe fallback in v3 (PR)
- chandra to add unit regression that runs packing+kernel transition at positions 4000..4100
- ben to audit memcpy/alignment changes in quant packing PR
sam: and add a CI longchain smoke (smaller seq but same transition logic) so we don't regress again.
ana: I'll open an issue with logs and tag the PRs. thanks all :heart:
